title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: C is a category and A a full subcategory. Grothendieck considers the composite f : C → Ĉ → Â = Hom(A°, Ens), sending X to the restricted representable Hom_C(-, X)|_A, i.e. the 'nerve' or restricted Yoneda functor.

Claim 1. If every X in C is a colimit in C of a diagram of objects of A, f is fully faithful. The parenthesis points to the canonical form X ≃ colim_{(Y→X), Y∈A} Y, the colimit over A/X. In modern terms: A is dense in C if and only if f is fully faithful.

Claim 2 (additive case). If C is additive, the same picture holds with additive presheaves: C → Ĉ_ab → Â_ab, where Â_ab is the category of additive functors A° → Ab. The forgetful functors ω_C : Ĉ_ab → Ĉ and ω_A : Â_ab → Â commute with the restrictions, and ω_A is faithful. Since ω_A ∘ f_ab = f, it follows that f_ab is fully faithful when f is. The margin note says the same holds for k-linear (or R-linear) structures. The bracket says this applies in particular when every X is isomorphic to a (finite) direct sum of objects of A.

Claim 3. Suppose further that every X is also a limit in C of objects of A. Then the essential image of C in Â (resp. Â_ab) lies in the full subcategory of presheaves that are such limits of representables. The next page completes this: if C is stable under the relevant limits, C is equivalent to that subcategory. The additive special case is C ≃ the full subcategory of Â_ab of finite direct sums of representables, i.e. add(A) seen as the finitely generated free (projective) A-modules.

Purpose. The previous page aims to determine the category of ∂-perfect half-simplicial complexes from a small full subcategory A, generated by the O(-) and the operations Ψ^i, together with A's '½-additive' structure. This page is the general categorical lemma justifying that C is known up to equivalence once A and its (semi-)additive structure are known.
errors: As literally stated, Claim 1 is false. Being a colimit of SOME diagram in A does not make f fully faithful; one needs X to be the CANONICAL colimit over A/X (density). Counterexample: C = Ab, A = {Z}. Every abelian group is a colimit of a diagram of copies of Z (e.g. Z/n = coequalizer of n, 0 : Z → Z). Yet f lands in sets with an action of the multiplicative monoid (Z,·), and non-additive maps commuting with scalar multiplication exist, so f is not full.

The bracket ('in particular if every X is a sum of objects of A') is presented as a case of the Set-valued hypothesis, but there f need not be fully faithful. Example: C = Ab, A = {Z}, X = Z⊕Z; there are non-additive (Z,·)-equivariant maps Z² → Z. The conclusion holds only for the additive functor f_ab, by additive Yoneda. So the route 'f fully faithful + ω_A faithful ⇒ f_ab fully faithful' is valid as an implication, but its hypothesis fails in exactly the additive situation of interest. The additive statement must be proved directly; it is true.
Minor: 'somme d'objets de C' and 'lim d'objets de C' must mean objects of A. The sums must be finite, as the next page specifies.

ideas.what: The restricted Yoneda functor C → Â is fully faithful when every object is the canonical colimit of objects of A over A/X.
ideas.modern_name: Dense subcategory / dense functor (restricted Yoneda embedding)
ideas.where_published: Closely related material on generating families and colimits of representables appears in SGA 4 Exposé I (Grothendieck–Verdier); unsure whether density is stated in exactly this form.

ideas.what: Additive/enriched version: f_ab : C → Add(A°, Ab) is fully faithful, deduced via faithfulness of the forgetful functor; the same for k-linear categories.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mitchell (1972, 'Rings with several objects'); Kelly (enriched category theory)

ideas.what: If every object is a finite direct sum of objects of A, then C is equivalent to the finitely generated free A-modules (finite sums of representables) in Â_ab; generally C is equivalent to presheaves that are limits/colimits of representables of a given type.
ideas.modern_name: Additive closure add(A) ≃ finitely generated free (projective) A-modules; Auslander's projectivization; reconstruction of a category from a dense subcategory

deep.surprise_reason: Standard density / additive Yoneda lemma, written as a tool for describing the category of ∂-perfect half-simplicial complexes by a small generating subcategory. Nothing new for specialists; the page even contains a minor imprecision (an arbitrary colimit vs the canonical colimit).
transcription_corrections: Margin note: likely 'idem pour structures k-lin. (ou R-lin.) sur C', not 'item pour structures f-lin.'.
'somme d'objets de C' and 'lim d'objets de C': as written, the letter may look like C, but mathematically these must be objects of A.
'Supposons de plus que tout X ∈ C soit aussi isom. à une lim←' ('sous.' is probably 'isom.').
'(mais pas unic. A)' is uncertain; possibly '(mais pas univ.)' or a remark that the diagram is not unique.
In the diagram, the lower composite C → Ĉ → Â is labelled r (with r_ab above), and the restriction arrows are 'rest f' / 'rest f_ab'.
